text: Retroactivity describes the phenomenon in which an upstream genetic circuit changes the behavior of a downstream circuit, but downstream circuits never affect upstream dynamics.
explanation: This is false and reverses the actual direction: retroactivity specifically describes how a downstream circuit (e.g., its binding sites titrating away an upstream transcription factor) changes the dynamics of the upstream circuit that drives it, analogous to a low-impedance electronic load dropping the output voltage of an amplifier. Upstream-to-downstream signaling is the normal, intended direction of information flow in a circuit, not what the term retroactivity refers to.
